note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 (independent auditor, after d3195edb70 rewrote the row annotation and openV6 changed on 2026-10-27): RFC 9568 Section 5.1.2.3 says "The Hop Limit MUST be set to 255." openV6 (internal/plugins/vrrp/transport/backend_linux.go) still sets IPV6_MULTICAST_HOPS 255 on the advertisement tx socket, and advertisements go only to ff02::12 through SendAdvert's Sendmsg on that socket, so the multicast hop limit is the one every advertisement carries; openNASocket sets the same on the NA socket. TestIntegrationOpenInstanceSocketOptions (//go:build linux, opens with userns.Enter, which runs it unprivileged in its own user, network and mount namespace and carries the child's fail or skip back) reads IPV6_MULTICAST_HOPS back with getsockopt from both the tx and NA socket and requires exactly 255; the kernel default is 1, so an openV6 that stopped setting it fails, and the recorded mutant (255 -> 254 in openV6) went red. Single-polarity per the row annotation: a socket constant no input changes; receive-side discard is the separate -5.1.2.3-2 row. The rewritten annotation now matches the test. Findings outside this verdict: the tag's claim still cites backend_linux.go:185 where the call is now at :187, and the summary's Support remaining text still calls this evidence integration-gated, QEMU-only and unreachable by ./le rfc record, which is no longer true. Verdict enforced.
